# MCP gateway endpoint

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P4 · Agents everywhere](../README.md#phase-4--agents-everywhere) · **Lane:** Worker · **Label:** `feature:mcp-gateway` · **Epic:** [#191](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/191) · **Tickets:** 17 (7S 10M)

Workers expose MCP gateways at `https://mcp.warden.internal/mcp/{gateway}`, served inside the existing proxy path so the agent reaches them through its identity forwarder and never holds a Warden token. Each gateway bundles several upstream MCP servers from the registry, presents one namespaced tool list, routes calls to the right upstream, and applies the existing verdict engine, secret swap and per-user credentials exactly once per call, so agents get a single MCP URL instead of many.

## How we build it

- Scope and flag: new package internal/mcp/hub; internal/mcp/gateway stays the only verdict engine. New worker-local block `mcpGateway: {enabled: false, host: mcp.warden.internal, maxSessions: 1024, maxSessionsPerUser: 16, sessionIdleTTL: 30m, maxUpstreamSessions: 4096, listTimeout: 5s, callTimeout: 60s, stdio: {enabled: false, maxProcesses: 16, runAsUID, runAsGID, idleStopAfter: 15m}}`. With it off, a CONNECT to that host is evaluated like any other destination (default-deny) and worker and bundle behaviour are byte-identical. The hub needs `mcp.enabled` and a verified signed bundle (W-P2-SBND-04); standalone workers are unsupported in v1.
- Transport and auth through the existing proxy path, not a new listener. The agent configures `https://<mcpGateway.host>/mcp/{gateway}` and keeps HTTPS_PROXY pointed at the identity forwarder (W-P2-RCP-02), so it never holds a Warden token. handleConn (internal/proxy/serve.go) intercepts a CONNECT to the reserved host after identity extraction, agent_disabled, require mode 407 (W-P2-WBND-03), the block list (W-P1-BLOCK-02) and agent binding (W-P2-WBND-02), and before policy.Evaluate or any dial. It terminates TLS with a proxy-CA leaf and passes each request plus the connIdentity to the hub. The hub accepts only a valid, agent-bound Warden identity (no anonymous mode in v1); failures on this terminated path are 403 JSON as W-P2-WBND-03 requires, never 401 or WWW-Authenticate.
- Protocol: POST and DELETE on /mcp/{gateway}; GET returns 405 (no server-initiated stream in v1). A non-empty Origin header gets 403 (DNS-rebinding guard). MCP-Protocol-Version is checked against the fixed list chosen in the W-P4-MGW-01 ADR, which matches the revision constant W-P3-JIT-03 records in internal/connect. Batches get -32600 and the body is capped at 1 MiB. Only tools are proxied: initialize, ping, notifications/initialized, tools/list and tools/call are handled; every other method returns -32601.
- Sessions: Mcp-Session-Id is 128-bit crypto/rand, bound to (idp_iss, sub, agent, gateway) and never to a token jti, so a token rotated by the forwarder keeps the session. Idle TTL on the monotonic clock, caps maxSessions and maxSessionsPerUser (429 on initialize), LRU eviction, DELETE ends a session. An unknown, evicted or other-identity id returns 404 and the client re-initializes, as the spec allows. Multi-replica workers need sticky routing or accept re-initialization.
- Gateway definitions: CP table `mcp_gateways` {name slug, agents[] (required, non-empty), servers[{registryId, tools[] (explicit, non-empty)}], created_by, updated_by, updated_at}, CRUD at `/dashboard/api/mcp/gateways` with the `mcp:read`/`mcp:write` scopes from W-P4-MREG-02 and an admin audit record on every write. Shipped as the signed-bundle section `mcpGateways` (omitted when empty) with publish_log reason `mcp_gateway`. A worker serves only gateways that list its bound agent (W-P2-AREG-05); others return 404. Later registry changes never fail a bundle: tools that drop out are removed at runtime and the API reports `stale_tools`. Deleting a referenced registry server returns 409.
- Effective tools and naming: effective = gateway selection ∩ current registry approvedTools ∩ grant `tools` claim when present. The hub enforces this as a hard allow-list whatever `mcp.mode` is; monitor mode only decides whether policy and scan findings block a tool already in that set. Client-facing names are `<registryId>__<tool>`, split on the first `__`; registry ids used by gateways may not contain `__` or `:`, and names are capped at 128 characters. The verdict engine evaluates the bare upstream name, so existing `mcp.tools` rules apply as for proxied MCP, and it also matches rules and grant entries written as `server__tool`; a deny in either form wins. Inventory and schema profiles from the hub are keyed by (server, tool); rate-limit counters stay keyed by the configured rule name, so a limit on a bare name counts calls to every server.
- Verdicts: tools/list fans out in parallel with listTimeout per upstream. Each upstream's raw result goes through the verdict engine's response check (inventory, poisoning, W-P4-MREG-06 registry pins); tools named in blocking findings or outside the effective set are dropped, and one slow or failing upstream drops only its own tools and records finding mcp_upstream_unavailable. Listings are cached per (server, registry version) for 60s and dropped on bundle apply. tools/call runs `OnRequest(..., gateway.RequestMeta{Subject, GatewayServer})` (the W-P1-GPOL-04 seam; GrantID and GrantTools ride on identity.Subject as W-P4-DGR-05 defines, so there is no second OnRequest variant) with session key `<agent>:<gateway>:<userKey>:<registryId>` so serverFromSessionKey still yields the server and chain analysis never mixes users. The hub reads the live engine on every call because SettingsApplier.Apply rebuilds and closes it; a nil engine, panic or parse error on tools/call is a deny. A deny returns a JSON-RPC error with the client's id and nothing reaches the upstream; a result over mcp.maxResponseScanBytes is denied, not passed unscanned.
- Upstream egress without a second verdict: HTTP and SSE upstreams use an in-process connection, not TCP loopback. The hub transport dials a net.Pipe served by a new `Proxy.ServeInternal(conn, origin)`. The typed InternalOrigin {gateway, server, identity holder} can only be set from Go code. Internal-origin traffic runs the allowlist, SafeDialer, static and per-user secret swap, DLP, response redaction, JIT and recordEvent unchanged; it skips mcpRequestScan and the response verdict because the hub already ran them, so each call is evaluated and rate-counted exactly once. One transport per (userKey, server) so a tunnel never carries another user's call. Upstream URL and credential header come only from the signed registry: new registry-version field `auth: {header, placeholder}` holds a placeholder name only, and changing it is a widening change.
- Per-user credentials: an upstream is per-user when its `auth.placeholder` is a perUserSecrets mapping placeholder; the CP checks that the upstream host is in mapping.domains and the gateway's agents are in mapping.agents. The swap goes through the existing W-P3-PUS-04 stage and worker UserTokenSource (W-P3-PUS-09), never a second token path, and events record Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10). A missing grant comes back as the W-P3-JIT-03 JSON-RPC answer; the hub restores the client's id, and where it must answer itself it uses the internal/connect MCPToolResult/MCPError builders. Users without a grant see the last pin-verified cached tool list, so a call can trigger consent. Parking is W-P4-PARK-05.
- Stdio upstreams (behind `mcpGateway.stdio.enabled`, default false): the registry entry must carry sha256 or ed25519 integrity. The worker copies the binary into a private 0700 directory, verifies the copy with stdio.VerifyBinary/VerifyEd25519 and executes that copy, so it cannot be swapped between check and launch. Stdio is off by default in v1. The child runs as a distinct `runAsUID/GID`, which needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID; that capability is a documented opt-in for operators who set `stdio.enabled`, and is never part of the default hardened image (`USER warden`, no added capabilities). A separate stdio runner container is P5 Helm work. The child gets only PATH, HOME (private temp dir), SSL_CERT_FILE (worker CA public cert), registry env names set to placeholder values, and HTTPS_PROXY pointing at a per-process loopback listener with a random credential that maps to an internal origin, where the worker swaps static placeholders on egress. The worker environment is never inherited. Per-user credentials on stdio are out of scope in v1 and rejected by CP validation. Residual risk, documented: a stdio child can ignore HTTPS_PROXY and dial out directly; network confinement is P5 deployment work, and binaries and the added capability belong in an operator-built derived worker image.
- Recording and observability: each hub tools/call stores one decision event through recordEvent with Protocol `mcp`, Tool = bare tool name and new omitempty fields MCPGateway and MCPServer; the internal-origin egress event carries the same fields. Fleet-store columns are a separate CP ticket. Metrics: `warden.mcp_gateway.sessions`, `warden.mcp_gateway.calls.total{gateway,server,outcome}`, `warden.mcp_gateway.upstream.duration{server}`, `warden.mcp_gateway.stdio.restarts.total{server}` and stage=mcp_gateway in warden.request.added_latency; labels are bounded by the bundle, with no sub or agent. No token, tool argument or result body appears in logs.
- Degraded modes and rollout: with the CP down the hub keeps serving from the last-known-good bundle, and per-user tokens work until the UserTokenSource cache TTL, then calls get a user_token_unavailable tool error. With the IdP down, existing Warden tokens work until exp (P2 rules). A worker restart drops sessions (clients re-initialize) and stdio children restart on first use. Only relative expiries and monotonic timers are used. Workers advertise heartbeat cap `mcpgateway/v1`. Upgrade the CP first, then workers.
- Upstream lifecycle and agent setup: stdio children start lazily on the first tools/list or tools/call and stop with a clean SIGTERM after `mcpGateway.stdio.idleStopAfter` (default 15m, 0 = never); an idle stop is not a crash and never counts toward the restart/down rule, and while a child is stopped its last pin-verified tools/list answers lists. An upstream `notifications/tools/list_changed` drops that server's cached listing and triggers one re-list; the new list passes the registry pin and drift checks (W-P4-MREG-06/09) before any new tool becomes callable, and the notification is never forwarded to the agent. Idle HTTP and SSE upstream sessions get a JSON-RPC `ping` every 60s with ±20% jitter; failures feed the existing breaker, and a server that answers -32601 is not pinged again for that session. Workers report per-server state up|down|breaker_open with a bounded last error class, shown in the console and readable through the CP API. initialize advertises `tools.listChanged:false` while GET returns 405; an opt-in GET SSE stream (default off, bounded per agent) turns it on and pushes list_changed to agents. Operators get a ready client config from `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways/{name}/client-config` or `warden mcp config <gateway>`, built from CP config (never the request Host header) and holding no token, key or query string.

## Done when

On a compose deployment with signed bundles, the token service, perUserSecrets and `mcpGateway.enabled` on, a require-mode worker is bound to agent A, whose container reaches Warden only through the identity forwarder and holds no Warden token. Configured with the single URL `https://mcp.warden.internal/mcp/{gateway}`, A's MCP client lists namespaced tools from an HTTP upstream and a stdio upstream (stdio turned on through the documented opt-in: `mcpGateway.stdio.enabled`, runAsUID/GID and CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID; the default image runs with stdio off); users U1 and U2 each reach the HTTP upstream with their own per-user access token; and the stdio tool's egress gets a static placeholder swapped by the worker. A tool outside the gateway, registry or grant set is blocked with no upstream contact even in monitor mode, and a tool denied by `mcp.tools` is blocked by the same verdict engine as proxied MCP traffic. A registry pin mismatch drops that tool, an upstream host not on the allowlist gives a tool error, and a user with no grant gets the authorization_required tool result with their own request id. Each call is evaluated and rate-counted exactly once and recorded with gateway, server, user_sub and act; no token appears in the agent container, logs or events; with the CP stopped the gateway keeps serving from its last-known-good bundle; and with `mcpGateway` off the worker and bundle are byte-identical to before. An idle stdio upstream stops after `idleStopAfter` and restarts on the next call without counting as a crash; an upstream tools/list_changed makes a newly added tool callable only after it passes its registry pin; and `warden mcp config <gateway>` prints a client config for the gateway URL that contains no token or key.

### 1/17 · W-P4-MGW-01

**Spike: choose the MCP transport layer and confirm agent clients honour HTTPS_PROXY**

Type **spike** · Size **S** · Issue [#192](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/192)

Decide between modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk and a hand-rolled JSON-RPC layer for the hub's Streamable HTTP server and its HTTP, legacy SSE and stdio clients. The deciding criterion is that the verdict engine sees the raw bytes on the wire and the hub can rewrite `params.name` and `id` without re-encoding other fields. The spike also confirms that the Claude Code and Codex MCP HTTP transports send their traffic through HTTPS_PROXY, because the gateway is served inside the proxy path; if they do not, that is recorded as a blocker, not solved by giving the agent a token.

**Requirements**

- Compare both options for: server Streamable HTTP (JSON or single-event SSE reply, Mcp-Session-Id, DELETE, 405 on GET), client Streamable HTTP, legacy HTTP+SSE and newline stdio. Record license, number of new go.mod modules, binary size delta and govulncheck result.
- Hard requirement: raw json.RawMessage per message is available for gateway.OnRequest/OnResponse, and the hub can rewrite `params.name` and `id` without changing other bytes.
- Pin a single MCP spec revision equal to the revision constant W-P3-JIT-03 adds to internal/connect, and record the supported MCP-Protocol-Version list, batch handling (-32600) and how upstream JSON-RPC ids are multiplexed and mapped back.
- The SSE response path reuses internal/mcp/sse.Scan, or the ADR states why it cannot.
- Check with the real Claude Code and Codex CLIs that an HTTP MCP server URL is reached through HTTPS_PROXY (CONNECT to the reserved host); record the CLI versions tested and any setting needed.
- Prototype code lives only in a _test.go file and adds no go.mod dependency unless the ADR chooses the SDK; nothing is wired into the worker.

**Implementation plan**

1. Create docs/adr/ (new directory) and docs/adr/0001-mcp-gateway-transport.md (new).
2. Prototype both options in new internal/mcp/hub/spike_test.go: initialize, notifications/initialized and tools/list against an httptest Streamable HTTP server, and parse an SSE reply with sse.Scan.
3. Feed the raw tools/list body to gateway.OnResponse and a tools/call with rewritten params.name and id to gateway.OnRequest, and byte-compare to show only name and id changed.
4. Run Claude Code and Codex in a container with HTTPS_PROXY set to a test forwarder and an MCP server URL on a non-resolvable host; record whether a CONNECT arrives.
5. Write the ADR: chosen layer, pinned revision, protocol version list, GET/batch/Origin behaviour, id remapping, client HTTPS_PROXY findings, license and go.mod delta.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] docs/adr/0001-mcp-gateway-transport.md exists and names the chosen approach, the pinned MCP revision (equal to the internal/connect constant), the license and the go.mod delta (0 modules if hand-rolled).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub/... -run TestSpikeInitializeListTools` passes: initialize and tools/list against an httptest server return the tool names.
- [ ] The spike test shows by byte comparison that rewriting params.name and id changes no other bytes of the message passed to gateway.OnRequest.
- [ ] The ADR records, per CLI and version, whether Claude Code and Codex send HTTP MCP traffic through HTTPS_PROXY.
- [ ] If the SDK is chosen, `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck ./...` reports no findings for the new modules.

### 2/17 · W-P4-MGW-02

**Add the MCP gateway definitions store and /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways API**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#193](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/193)

Add CP state for gateway definitions: which agents may use a gateway and which registry servers and tools it bundles. This ticket is CP-only and covers the store, REST API, validation against the registry and admin audit; bundle distribution is W-P4-MGW-09 and worker parsing is W-P4-MGW-10. A gateway can only narrow what the registry already approves, so writes need no approval gate.

**Requirements**

- New table `mcp_gateways` on CP SQLite state (migration): name slug ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$, agents JSON (non-empty list of agent ids), servers JSON [{registryId, tools[]}], created_by, updated_by, updated_at. At most 32 servers per gateway and 256 tools per server.
- Routes: GET/POST /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways and GET/PUT/DELETE /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways/{name}, registered as Scope-classified authz rows with `mcp:read` for reads and `mcp:write` for writes (same scopes as W-P4-MREG-02), so the W-P2-APIK-02 coverage test passes.
- Validation: each registryId exists, has a current version and contains neither `__` nor `:`; tools is an explicit non-empty list with no wildcard and each entry is in that version's approvedTools; no duplicate registryId; every agent id is registered (W-P2-AREG). Errors are 400 {error, field, index}.
- Registry stdio servers whose auth placeholder is a perUserSecrets mapping are rejected (per-user stdio is out of scope in v1).
- Registry interaction: deleting a registry server referenced by a gateway returns 409 naming the gateways; a registry rollback that removes a tool is never blocked, and GET returns `stale_tools` for the affected gateway.
- Every write records an admin audit entry (mcp.gateway.create|update|delete) with name, agent ids and server ids only.
- No bundle or worker change in this ticket; with the table empty, CP behaviour and /policy bytes are unchanged.
- Registry servers with transport `ws` are rejected (400 with field servers[i].registryId): the hub has HTTP, SSE and stdio connectors only in v1.

**Implementation plan**

1. New package internal/mcpgateways: `Gateway{Name, Agents []string, Servers []Server{RegistryID, Tools []string}}`, `Store` interface (List, Get, Put, Delete) and the SQLite implementation on cpstate with a migration.
2. New internal/mcpgateways/validate.go: Validate(g, registry mcpregistry.Store, agents) returning field-level errors; StaleTools(g, registry) for the GET view.
3. New internal/controlplane/mcp_gateways.go: handlers for the five routes, authz rows with Scope mcp:read/mcp:write, and admin audit through the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware.
4. internal/controlplane registry delete path (W-P4-MREG-02): return 409 when a gateway references the server.
5. Tests: internal/mcpgateways/store_test.go and internal/controlplane/mcp_gateways_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestMCPGatewayValidation` passes: an unknown registry id returns 400 with field servers[0].registryId, a tool outside approvedTools returns 400, an empty tools list returns 400 and an empty agents list returns 400.
- [ ] A viewer session or an API key without mcp:write gets 403 on POST, PUT and DELETE; an editor's create writes one admin audit entry with action mcp.gateway.create.
- [ ] Deleting registry server `gh` while gateway `dev` references it returns 409; after a registry rollback that removes `search`, GET /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways/dev lists `search` in stale_tools.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcpgateways/...` passes, and the W-P2-APIK-02 route coverage test passes with the new routes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MREG-02`](mcp-registry.md#211--w-p4-mreg-02) Add registry REST API with versioning, diff and rollback; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#28--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations through audit middleware; [`W-P2-APIK-02`](api-keys.md#27--w-p2-apik-02) Authenticate API keys and enforce per-route scopes in the authz table

### 3/17 · W-P4-MGW-03

**Serve /mcp/{gateway} on the reserved proxy host with sessions**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#194](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/194)

Create internal/mcp/hub with the Streamable HTTP handler and session manager, and serve it inside the proxy path: a CONNECT to `mcpGateway.host` is terminated by the worker after all CONNECT-time identity checks instead of being dialed. This keeps the P2 rule that the agent never holds a Warden token, since the forwarder injects it on CONNECT as today. tools/list and tools/call are stubs until W-P4-MGW-06.

**Requirements**

- New worker-local config block `mcpGateway` in internal/config: enabled (false), host (mcp.warden.internal), maxSessions (1024), maxSessionsPerUser (16), sessionIdleTTL (30m), maxUpstreamSessions (4096), listTimeout (5s), callTimeout (60s), stdio {enabled false, maxProcesses 16, runAsUID, runAsGID}. stdio stays off by default in v1, and with it off the worker needs no capability beyond the default hardened image. enabled requires mcp.enabled and a controlPlane endpoint with signed bundles; otherwise config load fails with a named error.
- In handleConn (internal/proxy/serve.go), a CONNECT to mcpGateway.host:443 is intercepted only after agent_disabled, require-mode 407, the block list and agent binding, and before policy.Evaluate or any dial. TLS is terminated with a proxy-CA leaf for the host. With mcpGateway off the host is evaluated like any other destination.
- The hub accepts a request only with a valid, agent-bound Warden identity on the CONNECT (TokenType warden, act.sub == bound agent); otherwise 403 JSON {error: identity_required}. No 401 or WWW-Authenticate is written (W-P2-WBND-03), and a request after the identity's exp gets 403 identity_expired.
- Handler on /mcp/{gateway}: POST takes one JSON-RPC message (batch -32600, body over 1 MiB 413); DELETE ends the session (204); GET 405. Non-empty Origin gets 403; an MCP-Protocol-Version not in the ADR list gets 400. Unknown gateways, or gateways that do not list the bound agent, get 404.
- Sessions: initialize returns a 128-bit crypto/rand Mcp-Session-Id bound to (idp_iss, sub, agent, gateway), the pinned protocolVersion and capabilities {tools:{listChanged:false}} (false because GET returns 405 and the hub pushes nothing; W-P4-MGW-16 turns it on when its stream is enabled). Reuse with another identity or gateway, or after eviction, gets 404. Idle TTL on an injectable monotonic clock, LRU at maxSessions, 429 on initialize at maxSessionsPerUser.
- initialize, ping and notifications/initialized are handled; resources/*, prompts/*, completion/* and unknown methods return -32601; tools/list and tools/call return -32603 until W-P4-MGW-06.
- Metrics gauge warden.mcp_gateway.sessions and stage=mcp_gateway in warden.request.added_latency; logs carry gateway, agent and an 8-hex hash of the session id, never the token or raw session id.
- Session lookup and auth add under 1ms p99 on the cached verifier path.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/config/mcpgateway.go: MCPGatewayConfig on config.Policy as `MCPGateway`, defaults and validation; config tests.
2. New internal/mcp/hub/session.go: SessionManager with ids, binding, idle TTL, LRU, per-user cap and an OnClose hook for later upstream cleanup.
3. New internal/mcp/hub/handler.go: `hub.New(Options{Gateways func() map[string]Gateway, AgentID string, ...})` implementing http.Handler with the method, Origin, version and size checks.
4. internal/proxy/serve.go handleConn: new branch for the reserved host after the identity, block-list and binding checks; new internal/proxy/hubhost.go terminates TLS and serves the hub handler with the connIdentity in the request context.
5. internal/proxy/proxy.go: add `SetMCPHub(http.Handler)` (atomic, nil = off) following the SetMCPGateway pattern; internal/worker wires it when mcpGateway.enabled.
6. Tests: internal/mcp/hub/handler_test.go and session_test.go; internal/proxy/hubhost_test.go for interception order and the off path.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestInitializeSession` passes: POST initialize to /mcp/dev returns 200, an Mcp-Session-Id of 22+ base64url characters and result.capabilities.tools with listChanged false.
- [ ] A session created by sub alice, reused with bob's identity, returns 404; the same request after DELETE also returns 404; POST /mcp/unknown returns 404 and an Origin of https://evil.example returns 403.
- [ ] With maxSessionsPerUser 16, the 17th initialize by one sub returns 429 while another sub can still initialize.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestHubHostInterception` shows a CONNECT to the reserved host without a bound Warden token gets 407 in require mode and is never dialed, and with mcpGateway off the host is denied by policy like any unlisted domain.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/config -run TestMCPGatewayConfig` rejects enabled without mcp.enabled, and a config without the block parses to the same Policy as before.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MGW-01`](mcp-gateway.md#117--w-p4-mgw-01) Spike: choose the MCP transport layer and confirm agent clients honour HTTPS_PROXY; [`W-P4-MGW-10`](mcp-gateway.md#1017--w-p4-mgw-10) Verify and apply the mcpGateways bundle section on the worker; [`W-P2-WBND-03`](identity-enforcement.md#310--w-p2-wbnd-03) Enforce identity require mode on CONNECT and terminated traffic

### 4/17 · W-P4-MGW-04

**Add HTTP and SSE upstream connectors over the internal origin**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#195](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/195)

Implement the hub's `Upstream` interface for Streamable HTTP and legacy HTTP+SSE servers. Their transport dials `Proxy.ServeInternal` (W-P4-MGW-11) through net.Pipe, so the allowlist, secret swap, DLP and audit apply while the MCP verdict runs only once, in the hub. Default-deny holds: an upstream not on the allowlist fails with a tool error and the hub has no other dialer.

**Requirements**

- `Upstream` in internal/mcp/hub: Initialize(ctx) error, ListTools(ctx) (json.RawMessage, error) returning the raw tools/list result, CallTool(ctx, raw json.RawMessage) (json.RawMessage, error) and Close() error.
- Transport: Proxy=nil, DialContext returns a ServeInternal pipe carrying InternalOrigin{Gateway, Server, identity holder}, RootCAs = worker CA only, no redirect following. One transport per (userKey, server), so a pooled tunnel never carries another user's call. Only https upstream URLs.
- Streamable HTTP: POST with Accept application/json and text/event-stream, Mcp-Session-Id tracking, re-initialize once on 404; SSE replies parsed with internal/mcp/sse.Scan. Legacy SSE: the `endpoint` event must resolve to the same scheme and host as the registry URL, else mcp_upstream_invalid.
- Upstream credential: when the registry version has `auth` (W-P4-MGW-12), the hub sets `auth.header` to the placeholder name only; the proxy swap replaces it on the wire. The hub never holds a secret value.
- Limits: dial 5s, list listTimeout, call callTimeout. tools/list follows nextCursor up to 10 pages or 1,000 tools. A result over mcp.maxResponseScanBytes becomes tool error response_too_large and is never passed through. Reconnect with exponential backoff 250ms to 30s with jitter; a breaker opens for 30s after 5 consecutive failures.
- Upstream server-to-client requests (sampling/createMessage, elicitation/create, roots/list) get JSON-RPC -32601 and a finding; only notifications/progress for an in-flight call is passed back, other notifications are dropped, except notifications/tools/list_changed, which the hub consumes as described below and never forwards.
- A proxy deny or upstream error becomes a JSON-RPC tool error with a bounded reason and no upstream body content. Metric warden.mcp_gateway.upstream.duration{server}.
- tools/list_changed: an upstream `notifications/tools/list_changed` fires the connector's OnToolsChanged callback, which drops that server's cached listing and schedules one re-list (coalesced, at most one per server per second). The re-listed raw result goes through the same verify hook as any tools/list (wired by W-P4-MGW-06 to OnResponseMeta, so W-P4-MREG-06 pins and W-P4-MREG-09 drift checks run) before it replaces the last pin-verified set; until then a tool that appeared only in the new list is not callable.
- Keepalive: an HTTP or SSE upstream session idle for 60s (±20% jitter, injectable clock) is sent a JSON-RPC `ping` with listTimeout. A failure or timeout counts toward the existing breaker exactly like a failed call; a -32601 answer is not a failure and stops pings for that upstream session until it re-initializes. Pings never open a session that does not exist yet and are not counted as calls.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcp/hub/upstream.go: Upstream interface, id-remapping pending map and the shared transport builder using proxy.ServeInternal.
2. New internal/mcp/hub/upstream_http.go: Streamable HTTP client with session tracking, SSE parsing via sse.Scan and pagination.
3. New internal/mcp/hub/upstream_sse.go: legacy HTTP+SSE client with endpoint host check and id correlation.
4. New internal/mcp/hub/backoff.go: backoff and breaker with an injectable clock.
5. Tests: internal/mcp/hub/upstream_http_test.go and upstream_sse_test.go using an httptest TLS fake behind an in-process proxy.New.
6. internal/mcp/hub/upstream.go: add OnToolsChanged(func()) to Upstream and the coalesced re-list scheduler; new internal/mcp/hub/keepalive.go: jittered idle ping feeding the breaker in backoff.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestHTTPUpstreamInternalOrigin` passes: a CallTool to an allowlisted fake stores one egress event with mcp_gateway and mcp_server set, and a counting fake verdict engine sees zero OnRequest calls from the proxy side.
- [ ] With the upstream host not on the allowlist, CallTool returns a tool error with reason policy and the fake records zero connections.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestSSEUpstream` passes: results are parsed, and an endpoint event pointing at another host fails with mcp_upstream_invalid.
- [ ] A 2 MiB upstream result with maxResponseScanBytes 1 MiB returns tool error response_too_large and no result bytes.
- [ ] An upstream sampling/createMessage request is answered with -32601 and never reaches the hub client; two subs calling the same server use two distinct internal connections (asserted by the fake).
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestToolsListChangedRelist` passes: after the fake sends notifications/tools/list_changed adding tool `create`, the cached listing is dropped, exactly one tools/list reaches the fake, and with the verify hook rejecting `create` on a pin mismatch it stays out of the callable set while existing tools keep working.
- [ ] With an injectable clock, an idle session gets a ping between 48s and 72s; three failed pings plus two failed calls open the breaker; a fake answering ping with -32601 receives no further pings and its breaker stays closed.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MGW-03`](mcp-gateway.md#317--w-p4-mgw-03) Serve /mcp/{gateway} on the reserved proxy host with sessions; [`W-P4-MGW-11`](mcp-gateway.md#1117--w-p4-mgw-11) Add Proxy.ServeInternal for in-process hub egress; [`W-P4-MGW-12`](mcp-gateway.md#1217--w-p4-mgw-12) Add the upstream auth header field to registry versions

**Unblocks:** [`W-P4-MGW-06`](mcp-gateway.md#617--w-p4-mgw-06) Aggregate tools/list and route tools/call with verdicts; [`W-P4-MGW-14`](mcp-gateway.md#1417--w-p4-mgw-14) Store MCP gateway fields and upstream state in the CP fleet store

### 5/17 · W-P4-MGW-05

**Add the stdio upstream connector with integrity, separate uid and swapped egress**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#196](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/196)

Implement the stdio `Upstream` behind `mcpGateway.stdio.enabled`, which is off by default in v1. Running the child as a separate uid needs CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID; that is a documented opt-in and is not added to the default hardened image. A stdio server is third-party code running on the worker, so it gets mandatory integrity checks on the exact file it executes, a separate uid, an environment with placeholder names only, and egress through an authenticated internal listener where the worker swaps static secrets. Direct egress that ignores HTTPS_PROXY remains a documented residual risk until P5 network confinement. Processes start lazily on first use and stop after an idle period, so a rarely used server does not hold a process and uid slot.

**Requirements**

- Only registry stdio entries with sha256 or ed25519 integrity are started. The worker copies the binary into a private 0700 directory, runs stdio.VerifyBinary and stdio.VerifyEd25519 on the copy and executes that copy, before every start and restart; a mismatch spawns nothing.
- The child runs as `mcpGateway.stdio.runAsUID/runAsGID` with Setpgid and its own temp HOME and cwd; the connector refuses to start (named error) if these are unset or equal the worker's own uid, or if the setuid fails because CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID was not granted (the error names the opt-in docs), so the child cannot read the worker CA key or secret store files.
- Environment from an explicit allowlist, never inherited: PATH, HOME, SSL_CERT_FILE (worker CA public cert), NO_PROXY empty, registry env names set to their placeholder names, and HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY pointing at a per-process loopback listener with a random credential. No real secret value is ever placed in the child env.
- That loopback listener accepts only CONNECT with the per-process credential and hands each connection to Proxy.ServeInternal with origin stdio:<server>, so allowlist, static swap, DLP and audit apply. Per-user placeholders are denied there (no identity), matching W-P3-PUS-04.
- Framing: newline JSON-RPC with the 8 MiB line cap from internal/mcp/stdio (export ReadLine/WriteLine). One process per registry server shared by all callers, ids multiplexed by the hub. Processes capped at stdio.maxProcesses.
- Lifecycle: on crash, in-flight calls get tool error mcp_upstream_crashed and the process restarts with backoff 1s to 60s; after 5 crash restarts in 5 minutes the server is marked down and its tools are dropped from lists. On shutdown the process group gets SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5s.
- Logs: stderr drained into a 64 KiB ring; only line counts at info, lines truncated to 512 bytes at debug; binary path, sha256 prefix and exit code logged, never env values. Counter warden.mcp_gateway.stdio.restarts.total{server}.
- Idle stop: new key `mcpGateway.stdio.idleStopAfter` (duration, default 15m, 0 = never, minimum 1m otherwise) in internal/config/mcpgateway.go. The process starts lazily on the first tools/list or tools/call that needs it (integrity re-checked on every start). After idleStopAfter with no in-flight call, measured on the monotonic clock, the supervisor sends SIGTERM to the process group (SIGKILL after 5s); this clean stop is not a crash, does not increment the restart counter or the warden.mcp_gateway.stdio.restarts.total counter, and never contributes to the down rule.
- While a process is idle-stopped, tools/list is answered from the last pin-verified listing cached for that (server, registry version) without starting it; with no cached listing the process is started. The next tools/call starts it again before forwarding. Per-user stdio stays out of scope in v1.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/mcp/stdio/pump.go: export readLine/writeLine as ReadLine/WriteLine with no behaviour change to the wedge.
2. New internal/mcp/hub/upstream_stdio.go: copy, verify and exec with SysProcAttr{Setpgid, Credential}, allow-listed env and id multiplexing.
3. New internal/mcp/hub/stdio_egress.go: per-process loopback CONNECT listener with a random credential feeding proxy.ServeInternal.
4. New internal/mcp/hub/supervisor.go: restart with backoff, down marking, process cap and shutdown on ctx done.
5. New test/fakes/cmd/fakemcp: stdio MCP fake that can dump its env and exit on command; built in TestMain into t.TempDir and hashed.
6. Tests: internal/mcp/hub/upstream_stdio_test.go.
7. internal/config/mcpgateway.go: add stdio.idleStopAfter with default and validation; internal/mcp/hub/supervisor.go: idle timer, lazy start and a clean-stop path kept separate from crash accounting.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestStdioIntegrityMismatch` passes: a registry sha256 that does not match the built fake spawns no process and returns an integrity error.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestStdioRestart -race` passes: killing the fake mid-call returns mcp_upstream_crashed within 1s and the next call succeeds after restart.
- [ ] The fake's env dump contains HTTPS_PROXY pointing at the loopback listener, SSL_CERT_FILE and placeholder values for registry env names, and no variable set only in the worker's own env.
- [ ] On Linux with runAsUID set (test skipped with a reason elsewhere or without CAP_SETUID), the fake fails to open a file readable only by the worker uid, and a CONNECT to the loopback listener without the credential gets 407.
- [ ] Cancelling the worker context terminates the process group within 6s and leaves no child processes; with stdio.enabled false a stdio registry entry is never started.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestStdioIdleStop -race` passes: with idleStopAfter 1m on an injectable clock the fake exits after the idle period via SIGTERM, a tools/list while stopped is served from the pin-verified cache without spawning, and the next tools/call restarts it with the restart counter unchanged.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MGW-03`](mcp-gateway.md#317--w-p4-mgw-03) Serve /mcp/{gateway} on the reserved proxy host with sessions; [`W-P4-MGW-11`](mcp-gateway.md#1117--w-p4-mgw-11) Add Proxy.ServeInternal for in-process hub egress; [`W-P4-MREG-05`](mcp-registry.md#511--w-p4-mreg-05) Publish the registry as a signed-bundle section

### 6/17 · W-P4-MGW-06

**Aggregate tools/list and route tools/call with verdicts**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#197](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/197)

Replace the W-P4-MGW-03 stubs: fan tools/list out to the gateway's upstreams, filter to the effective tool set, namespace names as `<registryId>__<tool>`, and route tools/call to the right upstream after the verdict engine allows it. The effective-tool filter is a hard allow-list enforced by the hub whatever `mcp.mode` is, so the new endpoint stays default-deny even when the engine is in monitor mode or fails open. One slow upstream drops only its own tools.

**Requirements**

- tools/list: parallel fan-out with listTimeout per upstream and listTimeout+1s overall. Each raw result goes through OnResponseMeta (W-P4-MGW-13) with session key `<agent>:<gateway>:<userKey>:<registryId>`; tools named in blocking findings are dropped (the whole server only when a blocking finding has no Tool). Results cached per (server, registry version) for 60s and dropped on bundle apply.
- Effective set = gateway tools ∩ registry approvedTools ∩ grant tools when present ∩ Gateway.ToolPermitted (W-P4-MGW-13, side-effect-free), so listing consumes no rate budget. The response has no nextCursor.
- tools/call: a name outside the effective set gets -32602 'unknown tool' with no upstream contact. Otherwise the hub rewrites params.name to the bare tool and id to a hub-assigned upstream id, runs OnRequest with gateway.RequestMeta{Subject (the verified subject, carrying GrantID and GrantTools from W-P4-DGR-05), GatewayServer}, forwards, runs OnResponseMeta on the result and restores the client's id.
- Fail closed in the hub path: a nil live engine (mcp disabled by bundle), a verdict panic or a parse error on tools/call is a deny. A deny returns a JSON-RPC error from new `mcp.BlockError(id, reason)` (moved from stdio.blockError; stdio output stays byte-identical) with the client's id.
- The hub reads the live engine on every request through new `(*proxy.Proxy).LiveMCPGateway()`; it never keeps a *gateway.Gateway across calls, because SettingsApplier.Apply closes the old one.
- An upstream timeout or error drops only that server's tools and records finding mcp_upstream_unavailable (new reason in internal/denyreason/reasons.go). Each tools/call stores one decision event with Protocol mcp, Tool (bare), MCPGateway, MCPServer, Reason, user_sub, act and GrantID.
- Metric warden.mcp_gateway.calls.total{gateway,server,outcome}. Hub overhead on tools/call excluding the upstream stays under 2ms p99.
- list_changed wiring: the connector verify hook from W-P4-MGW-04 is OnResponseMeta, so a re-list triggered by upstream notifications/tools/list_changed replaces the cached set only after registry pin and drift checks (W-P4-MREG-06/09); a tools/call for a tool that is not yet in the pin-verified set gets -32602 with no upstream contact.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/mcp: new blockerror.go with BlockError(id json.RawMessage, reason string) []byte; internal/mcp/stdio/pump.go calls it (golden test unchanged).
2. internal/proxy/proxy.go: add exported LiveMCPGateway() wrapping mcpGateway(), plus a hub-facing interface with OnRequest, OnResponseMeta and ToolPermitted.
3. New internal/mcp/hub/aggregate.go: errgroup fan-out, filtering, namespacing (split on first `__`, 128-char cap) and the list cache invalidated from the applier.
4. New internal/mcp/hub/route.go: tools/call routing, id remapping, verdict calls, fail-closed handling and decision events through the proxy recordEvent path.
5. Tests: internal/mcp/hub/aggregate_test.go and route_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestAggregateToolsList` passes: upstreams `gh` and `jira` both offering `search` list as `gh__search` and `jira__search`.
- [ ] With policy denying `delete_repo`, tools/call `gh__delete_repo` returns a JSON-RPC error 'blocked by warden: mcp_tool_denied' with the client's id and the fake upstream records zero calls; with mcp.mode monitor, a tool outside the gateway selection is still refused with -32602.
- [ ] With `jira` sleeping 10s and listTimeout 5s, tools/list returns within 6.5s with only gh tools and one event with reason mcp_upstream_unavailable and mcp_server jira.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestListDoesNotConsumeRateLimit` passes: with search=2/min, three tools/list calls then two tools/call succeed and the third call is denied.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestUpstreamIDRemap` passes: two subs sending id 1 concurrently each get their own result.
- [ ] With a grant whose tools are [gh__search], tools/list shows only gh__search and tools/call jira__search is denied with mcp_grant_scope; with a nil live engine every tools/call is denied and nothing is forwarded.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestListChangedRepin` passes: after list_changed adds `create` with a pin that does not match the registry, tools/call `gh__create` gets -32602 and the fake records zero calls; with a matching pin the same call succeeds after the re-list.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MGW-04`](mcp-gateway.md#417--w-p4-mgw-04) Add HTTP and SSE upstream connectors over the internal origin; [`W-P4-MGW-13`](mcp-gateway.md#1317--w-p4-mgw-13) Key gateway verdicts by server and add a side-effect-free tool check

### 7/17 · W-P4-MGW-07

**Use per-user credentials for gateway upstreams**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#198](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/198)

Give each user their own upstream session for registry servers whose `auth.placeholder` is a perUserSecrets mapping, and let the existing proxy stage swap the user's token on the internal origin. The hub never resolves or holds user access tokens: it reuses the worker UserTokenSource through W-P3-PUS-04, the internal/connect MCPToolResult/MCPError builders from W-P3-JIT-03, and Event.UserTokenProvider from W-P3-PUS-10, as the earlier phases asked. Parking is left to W-P4-PARK-05.

**Requirements**

- Per-user upstream sessions are keyed by (idp_iss, sub, registryId), shared ones by registryId, with an LRU cap `mcpGateway.maxUpstreamSessions` (default 4096). A per-user session closes when the user's last hub session ends or idles out, when a bundle raises that user's userGrantEpochs, or when the user is blocked.
- The internal origin carries the caller's current verified identity in an atomic holder that the hub updates before each call, so a token rotated by the forwarder is used on the next call and an expired snapshot is denied identity_expired. W-P3-PUS-04 checks (mapped domain, warden token, bound agent in mapping.agents) run unchanged.
- Swapped calls record Event.UserTokenProvider (W-P3-PUS-10) and leave Event.Provider empty. There is no second token path in internal/mcp/hub.
- Missing grant on tools/call: the internal origin returns the W-P3-JIT-03 JSON-RPC result; the hub restores the client's id and relays it. When initialize or tools/list to that upstream failed with -32042, the hub answers tools/call itself with connect.MCPToolResult carrying the same AuthorizationRequired body, and adds no new error shape.
- tools/list for a user without a grant serves the last pin-verified listing cached for that (server, registry version), so the agent can call a tool and receive authorize_url; with no cached listing the server's tools are omitted and mcp_upstream_unavailable is recorded.
- Per-user stdio upstreams are refused at runtime as well as at CP validation.
- Logs, events and errors carry provider, registryId and an 8-hex user-key hash only; never the Warden token, an access token, authorize_url query secrets or a status_token.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/mcp/hub/pool.go: upstream pool keyed by registryId or (iss, sub, registryId), LRU cap, close hooks from SessionManager.OnClose, the applier's epoch updates and block-list changes.
2. internal/mcp/hub/upstream.go: per-user transports carry an identity holder in InternalOrigin; the hub updates it from the request's connIdentity before each call.
3. New internal/mcp/hub/jit.go: detect the JIT-03 result and -32042 errors, restore ids, and build replies with connect.MCPToolResult/MCPError.
4. internal/mcp/hub/aggregate.go: serve the cached pin-verified listing for per-user servers when the user's upstream reports authorization_required.
5. Tests: internal/mcp/hub/pool_test.go and jit_test.go with a fake UserTokenSource and fake upstream.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestPerUserUpstreamSessions` passes: alice and bob calling gh__search produce two upstream sessions, each request carrying that user's token from the fake UserTokenSource.
- [ ] With bob having no grant, tools/call gh__search returns result.isError true with structuredContent.error authorization_required and authorize_url, echoing bob's client id, and the fake upstream records zero calls from bob.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestPerUserEventProvider` passes: alice's event has UserTokenProvider github and an empty Provider.
- [ ] A bundle raising alice's userGrantEpochs closes her upstream session and the next call opens a new one.

### 8/17 · W-P4-MGW-08

**E2E test the MCP gateway with fake upstreams**

Type **test** · Size **M** · Issue [#199](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/199)

Add fake Streamable HTTP and stdio MCP servers and an integration test that runs a worker with a signed bundle containing registry, gateways and perUserSecrets, then drives the gateway through the reserved host exactly as an agent behind the forwarder would. It proves single evaluation, default-deny, per-user swaps and that no token leaks.

**Requirements**

- test/fakes gains a Streamable HTTP MCP fake (TLS, tools/list and tools/call, switchable inputSchema for drift, recorded calls and received Authorization headers); the stdio fake test/fakes/cmd/fakemcp from W-P4-MGW-05 is reused with its sha256 written into the registry integrity.
- test/integration/mcp_gateway_test.go (build tag integration) starts an in-process worker with a test-key signed bundle carrying mcpRegistry, mcpGateways, policy, perUserSecrets and userGrantEpochs, plus a fake UserTokenSource and CP pending endpoint. The client sends CONNECT mcp.warden.internal:443 with a bound Warden token, as the forwarder does.
- Cases: (1) namespaced list from HTTP and stdio upstreams; (2) allowed call; (3) denied call with zero upstream calls; (4) schema change after pinning gives mcp_schema_drift with Detail `registry pin`; (5) per-user call without a grant gives authorization_required; (6) per-user success with a distinct token per sub; (7) unreachable upstream drops only its tools; (8) a tool outside the gateway selection is refused with mcp.mode monitor.
- Assertions read stored events: Protocol mcp, Tool (bare), mcp_gateway and mcp_server set, user_sub set, exactly one decision event and one rate-limit decrement per call, and no secret or token in any event or log line.
- Runs under `scripts/check.sh --integration` in under 60s with no external network or Docker.
- The stdio upstream in the CI integration case runs without `runAsUID` (the child runs as the worker's own user), so CI needs no added capability; the `runAsUID` path has its own test that skips unless CAP_SETUID is present.

**Implementation plan**

1. New test/fakes/mcphttp.go: Streamable HTTP MCP fake with recorded calls and switchable schemas.
2. New test/integration/mcp_gateway_test.go: bundle builder with internal/bundle signing, worker start-up, TestMain building fakemcp and hashing it.
3. Implement the eight cases as subtests sharing one worker, with a captured slog buffer.
4. Confirm scripts/check.sh --integration already runs ./test/integration/... and needs no change.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test -tags=integration ./test/integration -run TestMCPGateway -count=1` passes all eight cases.
- [ ] Stored events for the allowed call have mcp_gateway "dev", mcp_server "gh" and tool "search"; the denied call's event has Reason mcp_tool_denied.
- [ ] The schema drift case returns finding Kind mcp_schema_drift with Detail "registry pin" on the first tools/list after the fake's schema changes.
- [ ] A grep of captured worker logs and stored events for the fake access tokens and the Warden token finds zero matches.
- [ ] `scripts/check.sh --integration` runs the test and it completes in under 60s on CI.

### 10/17 · W-P4-MGW-10

**Verify and apply the mcpGateways bundle section on the worker**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#317](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/317)

Parse and validate the `mcpGateways` section in the worker's bundle verifier and hand the gateways for the worker's bound agent to the hub through an atomic getter. A bad section rejects the bundle and keeps last-known-good. Worker-only change; it also advertises the `mcpgateway/v1` heartbeat capability.

**Requirements**

- The bundle verifier (W-P2-SBND-04) parses Sections["mcpGateways"]: names unique and slug-shaped, registryIds present in the same bundle's mcpRegistry and free of `__` and `:`, tool lists non-empty. Any error rejects the whole bundle and keeps last-known-good.
- The applier stores only gateways whose agents include the worker's bound agent id (W-P2-AREG-05) and computes each server's tools as the intersection with the current registry approvedTools; tools outside it are dropped and logged once per bundle by name.
- The hub reads gateways through an atomic getter swapped on apply; the list cache from W-P4-MGW-06 is invalidated on every apply.
- RemoteProvider.Heartbeat adds cap `mcpgateway/v1` only when mcpGateway.enabled; old CPs ignore it.
- With the section absent or mcpGateway off, the applier and heartbeat are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/worker/mcpgateways.go: section type, parse and validate, filter by bound agent, intersection with the registry.
2. internal/worker/applier.go SettingsApplier.Apply: store the parsed gateways atomically next to the registry from W-P4-MREG-05 and fire an invalidation hook.
3. Heartbeat caps: add mcpgateway/v1 when enabled.
4. Tests in internal/worker: bad section keeps last-known-good, agent filtering, intersection, heartbeat cap.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/worker -run TestApplyMCPGateways` passes: a section referencing a registry id absent from the bundle is rejected and the previous gateways stay active.
- [ ] A gateway listing only agent B is not served by a worker bound to agent A.
- [ ] A gateway tool missing from the registry's approvedTools is dropped from the applied set while the rest of the gateway stays.
- [ ] The heartbeat includes mcpgateway/v1 only with mcpGateway.enabled true.

### 11/17 · W-P4-MGW-11

**Add Proxy.ServeInternal for in-process hub egress**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#318](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/318)

Add an in-process entry point to the proxy so hub upstream traffic goes through the full egress pipeline without a network hop and without a second MCP verdict. Looping back over TCP would run mcpRequestScan again (session key `agent:host` in internal/proxy/http.go), double rate limits and events, and give no unforgeable way to mark hub traffic. The typed origin can only be set from Go code.

**Requirements**

- New `InternalOrigin{Gateway, Server string; Identity *IdentityHolder}` and `(*Proxy).ServeInternal(conn net.Conn, o InternalOrigin)`; the hub feeds it one end of a net.Pipe. The origin cannot be set from any header or network input.
- Internal-origin connections start at CONNECT parsing and then run the block list, allowlist, SafeDialer, static secret swap, per-user swap (W-P3-PUS-04), DLP, response redaction, JIT and recordEvent unchanged; only mcpRequestScan and the MCP response verdict are skipped.
- IdentityHolder is an atomic pointer to a verified connIdentity snapshot (including the unexported raw token used by W-P3-PUS-04); each request reads it, and a snapshot past exp is denied identity_expired.
- analytics.Event gains MCPGateway (json mcp_gateway) and MCPServer (json mcp_server), omitempty, with addColumnIfAbsent columns in the local SQLiteStore; internal-origin events set them, other events stay byte-identical.
- With no caller of ServeInternal, proxy behaviour is unchanged; no config flag is needed because the entry point is only reachable from the hub, which is default off.

**Implementation plan**

1. New internal/proxy/internal_origin.go: InternalOrigin, IdentityHolder and ServeInternal, reusing handleConn's CONNECT and terminated-request path with an origin on the connection scope.
2. internal/proxy/http.go: skip mcpRequestScan and the MCP response verdict when the connection scope has an internal origin; stamp MCPGateway/MCPServer on events.
3. internal/analytics/analytics.go and the local SQLite store: add the two fields and columns.
4. Tests: internal/proxy/internal_origin_test.go and an analytics column round-trip test.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/proxy -run TestServeInternalSkipsMCPVerdictOnly` passes: a tools/call through ServeInternal triggers zero OnRequest calls on a counting fake engine while DLP and secret swap still apply.
- [ ] A request over a normal CONNECT with any X-Warden-* header cannot cause the MCP verdict to be skipped.
- [ ] A ServeInternal request to a host not on the allowlist is denied with reason policy and stores one deny event with mcp_gateway and mcp_server set.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestMCPGatewayColumns` round-trips both fields, and an older database gains the columns without data loss.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-WBND-02`](identity-enforcement.md#210--w-p2-wbnd-02) Bind Warden tokens to the worker's registered agent and key; [`W-P3-PUS-10`](refresh-model.md#1012--w-p3-pus-10) Record the per-user token provider on analytics events

### 12/17 · W-P4-MGW-12

**Add the upstream auth header field to registry versions**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#319](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/319)

HTTP and SSE upstreams need a declared header that carries a credential placeholder, and per-user detection needs to come from data rather than a separate flag. Add `auth: {header, placeholder}` to registry versions and to the `mcpRegistry` bundle entry; it holds a placeholder name only, never a value. A server is per-user exactly when its placeholder is a perUserSecrets mapping placeholder.

**Requirements**

- mcpregistry.Version gains optional Auth{Header, Placeholder}: header is a valid HTTP header name other than Host, Cookie or Proxy-*; placeholder must name a static `secrets[]` placeholder or a `perUserSecrets.mappings[].placeholder`.
- For a per-user placeholder the CP checks that the registry URL host is in mapping.domains (so the swap cannot fail with secret_domain_mismatch) and rejects stdio servers.
- Adding or changing auth is a widening change routed through the W-P4-MREG-03 approval gate; removing it is narrowing.
- The `mcpRegistry` bundle entry carries `auth` when set (omitted otherwise, so bundles without it are byte-identical), and the worker registry type parses it.
- Secret-looking values in placeholder are rejected with the same check MREG-01 applies to env.
- A per-user placeholder requires the version's `per_user_provider` (W-P4-MREG-01) to equal that mapping's provider, and a set per_user_provider requires a per-user auth placeholder; a mismatch returns 422 {field: auth.placeholder}, so the two fields can never disagree.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/mcpregistry: add Auth to Version, validation and the migration column.
2. internal/controlplane registry handlers: cross-check placeholders against secrets and perUserSecrets mappings; classify auth changes as widening.
3. Bundle builder and worker registry parser (W-P4-MREG-05 types): add the optional auth field.
4. Tests in internal/mcpregistry and internal/controlplane.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestRegistryAuthValidation` passes: an unknown placeholder returns 400, a per-user placeholder whose mapping.domains lacks the URL host returns 400, and a per-user placeholder on a stdio server returns 400.
- [ ] Adding auth to an approved server creates a pending approval instead of a new current version.
- [ ] A bundle for a registry without auth is byte-identical to before; one with auth round-trips through the worker parser.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MREG-03`](mcp-registry.md#311--w-p4-mreg-03) Route widening registry changes and rollbacks through approvals; [`W-P4-MREG-05`](mcp-registry.md#511--w-p4-mreg-05) Publish the registry as a signed-bundle section; [`W-P3-PUS-08`](refresh-model.md#812--w-p3-pus-08) Serve perUserSecrets and userGrantEpochs as signed-bundle sections

### 13/17 · W-P4-MGW-13

**Key gateway verdicts by server and add a side-effect-free tool check**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#320](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/320)

The verdict engine keys inventory and schema profiles by bare tool name, so two upstreams that both offer `search` would merge inventory and flap drift findings, and ToolPolicy.Evaluate consumes rate budget, so it cannot filter tools/list. Add server-aware variants used only by the hub, leaving the proxied MCP path's keys and behaviour unchanged.

**Requirements**

- Extend the W-P1-GPOL-04 `gateway.RequestMeta` with `GatewayServer string`; grant fields stay on identity.Subject (GrantID, GrantTools) as W-P4-DGR-05 defines, and no RequestContext or OnRequestCtx type is added. When set, policy, scopes and constraints match both the bare name and `server__tool`, a deny in either form wins, and grant tools match either form.
- Add `OnResponseMeta(meta gateway.RequestMeta, sessionKey, status, hdr, body)`; with GatewayServer set, inventory and schema profiles are keyed by (server, tool) and W-P4-MREG-06 registry pins are looked up by registry id.
- Rate-limit counters stay keyed by the configured rule name, so a bare-name limit counts calls to every server.
- Add `ToolPermitted(meta gateway.RequestMeta, tool string) bool` covering tool policy, scopes, grant tools and registry approvedTools, with no rate, session or inventory mutation.
- With GatewayServer empty, OnRequest, OnResponse and all existing keys are byte-for-byte unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/mcp/gateway/gateway.go: add GatewayServer handling in OnRequest, new OnResponseMeta and (server, tool) keys in recordInventoryLocked and the schema profiler.
2. internal/mcp/mcp.go: add a read-only ToolPolicy.Permitted(tool) that shares matching logic with Evaluate without touching counters.
3. internal/mcp/gateway: new ToolPermitted on Gateway combining policy, scopes, grant and registry checks.
4. Tests: internal/mcp/gateway/server_key_test.go and internal/mcp/mcp_test.go additions.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A rule denying `gh__search` blocks search on gh but not on jira; a rule denying bare `search` blocks both.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp -run TestPermittedNoSideEffects` passes: 100 Permitted calls leave the rate counter unchanged.
- [ ] Existing `go test ./internal/mcp/...` tests pass unchanged.

### 14/17 · W-P4-MGW-14

**Store MCP gateway fields and upstream state in the CP fleet store**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#321](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/321)

Workers send events with the new mcp_gateway and mcp_server fields from W-P4-MGW-11, but the CP fleet store has no columns for them. Add the columns and ingest so fleet queries and the console can filter by gateway and server. Workers also report per-server upstream state (up, down or breaker_open with the last error class) in the heartbeat, so operators can see an unhealthy upstream before agents report missing tools.

**Requirements**

- FleetSQLiteStore gains mcp_gateway and mcp_server columns via addColumnIfAbsent, following the W-P3-PUS-10 pattern.
- Fleet ingest stores both fields; events without them store empty values and existing rows are unaffected.
- Fleet query filters gain optional gateway and server parameters; values are bounded by bundle names.
- No change to the event wire format beyond W-P4-MGW-11; the only worker change is the heartbeat field below.
- Worker heartbeat adds `mcpUpstreams: [{server, state, lastErrorClass, ageSeconds}]`, at most 256 entries and only when mcpGateway.enabled. state is up|down|breaker_open: breaker_open while the W-P4-MGW-04 breaker is open, down when the W-P4-MGW-05 down rule fired or the last list or ping failed, otherwise up (an idle-stopped stdio server is up). lastErrorClass is one of timeout|connect|tls|policy|http_status|protocol|crashed|integrity, never message text, URL or body; ageSeconds is relative, not a wall-clock time.
- The CP keeps the latest state per (worker, server) in WorkerRegistry (memory only) and serves `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways/{name}/status` (Scope mcp:read, viewer, authz row) returning, per server in the gateway, the worst state across workers serving it, worker counts per state and the last error class. The console gateway view shows it, and the admin MCP server reads the same route with an mcp:read key.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go: add the columns, insert and filter support.
2. internal/controlplane fleet ingest and query handlers: accept and pass the fields.
3. Tests in internal/analytics and internal/controlplane.
4. New internal/mcp/hub/state.go: per-server state tracker fed by the breaker, the stdio supervisor and list/ping results; internal/worker heartbeat builder adds mcpUpstreams.
5. internal/controlplane heartbeat handler and WorkerRegistry: store mcpUpstreams; internal/controlplane/mcp_gateways.go: add the status route; internal/dashboard/index.html: state column in the gateway view.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestFleetMCPGatewayColumns` passes: both fields round-trip and an older fleet database gains the columns without data loss.
- [ ] A fleet query filtered by gateway `dev` returns only events with mcp_gateway dev.
- [ ] Ingest of an event without the fields stores empty values and returns 200.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/mcp/hub -run 'TestGatewayUpstreamStatus|TestUpstreamStateTracker'` passes: a worker reporting gh breaker_open with class timeout makes GET /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways/dev/status show gh breaker_open and timeout, and the heartbeat JSON contains no URL or error message text.

### 15/17 · W-P4-MGW-15

**Document MCP gateway setup for operators and agents**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#322](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/322)

Write the operator and agent-author guide for the MCP gateway, so teams can turn it on without reading the code. It covers agent configuration through the identity forwarder, the error contract, limits and the stdio residual risk.

**Requirements**

- New docs/mcp-gateway.md: what the gateway does, the `mcpGateway` config block with defaults, and the CP gateway API with request and response examples and status codes.
- Agent setup for Claude Code and Codex: the URL `https://mcp.warden.internal/mcp/{gateway}`, HTTPS_PROXY pointing at the forwarder, and the CLI versions confirmed in the W-P4-MGW-01 ADR; no Warden token in the agent.
- Naming and policy: `server__tool` names, bare versus namespaced rules, rate limits counted per rule name, and the effective-set rule that holds in monitor mode.
- Error contract: -32601, -32602, blocked-by-warden errors, authorization_required results, response_too_large and the 403/404/405/429 HTTP answers.
- Operations: sticky routing or re-initialization for multi-replica workers, degraded modes (CP down, restart, token expiry), metrics, and the stdio opt-in: off by default in v1; turning it on needs a derived worker image with the server binaries, runAsUID/GID and CAP_SETUID/CAP_SETGID, which the default hardened image does not grant; plus the residual direct-egress risk until P5 (separate stdio runner container and network confinement in the Helm chart).
- Link the page from docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md.
- Upstream lifecycle: `mcpGateway.stdio.idleStopAfter`, lazy start, idle stop versus crash restarts, list_changed re-pinning, upstream keepalive pings and the per-server up|down|breaker_open state.
- Packaging a stdio server: build it as one pinned artifact (exact version, committed lockfile, dependencies installed offline into the derived worker image or a single binary), hash it with sha256 or sign it with ed25519, pin its tools with `warden mcp inspect` (W-P4-MREG-09) and register the hash or signature. Warden never installs or fetches packages at runtime: launch commands such as `npx -y`, `uvx` or `pipx run` are rejected by registry validation (W-P4-MREG-01), and command, args and env are written by the operator for the built artifact, never copied from a package README.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write docs/mcp-gateway.md (new) from the merged tickets' config keys, endpoints and reasons.

3. Add links in docs/architecture.md and docs/control-plane.md.

### 16/17 · W-P4-MGW-16

**Stream tools/list_changed to agents over GET SSE**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#338](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/338)

In v1 GET on /mcp/{gateway} returns 405 and initialize advertises `tools.listChanged:false`, so agents only see new or removed tools when they list again. Add an opt-in server-to-client SSE stream on GET that sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` when a session's effective tool set changes, and advertise `listChanged:true` only while it is on. Default off; streams are bounded per agent.

**Requirements**

- New keys `mcpGateway.listChangedStream: {enabled: false, maxStreamsPerAgent: 4, keepalive: 25s}` in internal/config/mcpgateway.go. With enabled false, GET stays 405 and initialize keeps listChanged false, byte-identical to W-P4-MGW-03.
- With enabled true, initialize advertises capabilities.tools.listChanged true, and GET /mcp/{gateway} with Accept text/event-stream and a valid Mcp-Session-Id opens one SSE stream bound to that session's identity. The same Origin, MCP-Protocol-Version and identity checks as POST apply; a second stream on the same session gets 409 and a stream above maxStreamsPerAgent gets 429.
- The hub sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` on a stream when the session's effective tool set changes: after a re-list from upstream list_changed passes the pin checks (W-P4-MGW-04, W-P4-MGW-06), or after a bundle apply changes the gateway or registry. Notifications are coalesced to at most one per second and carry no tool names or upstream content.
- Stream lifetime: closed on session DELETE, idle eviction, the identity's exp (the forwarder drains the tunnel then and the client reconnects), and bundle apply that removes the gateway. A comment line is written every keepalive; a write that blocks for 5s closes the stream. No event replay (Last-Event-ID is ignored) in this ticket.
- Gauge warden.mcp_gateway.streams; logs carry gateway, agent and the 8-hex session hash only.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/mcpgateway.go: add the listChangedStream block, defaults and validation.
2. New internal/mcp/hub/notify.go: per-session stream registry with per-agent cap, coalescing and keepalive.
3. internal/mcp/hub/handler.go: GET branch when enabled and the listChanged capability flag on initialize.
4. internal/mcp/hub/aggregate.go: publish effective-set changes after a pin-verified re-list or bundle apply.
5. Tests: new internal/mcp/hub/notify_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcp/hub -run TestListChangedStream -race` passes.
- [ ] With the stream enabled, initialize returns listChanged true; after the upstream fake adds an approved tool with a matching pin, an open stream receives exactly one notifications/tools/list_changed within 2s.
- [ ] With the stream disabled, GET returns 405 and initialize returns listChanged false.
- [ ] With maxStreamsPerAgent 4, the fifth stream for the agent gets 429, and DELETE of a session closes its stream.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MGW-03`](mcp-gateway.md#317--w-p4-mgw-03) Serve /mcp/{gateway} on the reserved proxy host with sessions; [`W-P4-MGW-06`](mcp-gateway.md#617--w-p4-mgw-06) Aggregate tools/list and route tools/call with verdicts

### 17/17 · W-P4-MGW-17

**Generate agent MCP client config for a gateway**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#339](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/339)

Give operators a correct, copy-ready MCP client config for a gateway instead of hand-writing URLs. A CP route and `warden mcp config <gateway>` render the gateway URL for Claude Code, Codex or a generic client, the identity forwarder setup note and optional tool docs. The output is safe to paste into a repo: it holds no token, key or query string, and the host comes from CP config, never from the request.

**Requirements**

- Route `GET /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways/{name}/client-config?client=claude-code|codex|generic[&tools=true]` with an authz row (Scope mcp:read, viewer, not audited). Unknown client gives 400 {error: invalid, field: client}; unknown gateway gives 404. Response has Cache-Control: no-store.
- The URL is `https://<console.mcpGatewayHost>/mcp/<name>`, where new CP-local `console.mcpGatewayHost` (default mcp.warden.internal, a bare hostname with no port, path or query) must match the workers' `mcpGateway.host`. Host, X-Forwarded-Host and Origin request headers are never read.
- Response 200 {gateway, client, url, config, setup}: config is the client's snippet (claude-code: an `.mcp.json` mcpServers entry `warden-<name>` with type http and the url; codex: an `mcp_servers.warden-<name>` TOML table with the url, in the format recorded by the W-P4-MGW-01 ADR; generic: {url, transport: streamable-http}). setup says to run the client under `warden identity exec` or with HTTPS_PROXY pointing at `warden identity forward`, and that no Warden token is set in the client.
- tools=true adds tools[] {name (`server__tool`), server, pin (16-hex prefix)} for the gateway's tools that are in the registry's approved and pinned set, sorted by name. No upstream description text is copied, so nothing unverified enters the agent's context.
- The output never contains a Warden token, API key, session id, Proxy-Authorization value or any query string, and is deterministic for the same gateway and registry revision.
- CLI `warden mcp config <gateway> --client claude-code|codex|generic [--tools] --cp-url <url> [--cp-ca-file] [--api-key-file | --api-key-env (default WARDEN_API_KEY)]` calls the route, prints config to stdout and setup to stderr, and exits non-zero with the error on 400, 403 or 404.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/console.go: add mcpGatewayHost with default and hostname validation.
2. New internal/mcpgateways/clientconfig.go: pure Render(gateway, host, client, tools) for the three clients.
3. internal/controlplane/mcp_gateways.go: the client-config route and authz row.
4. New cmd/proxy/mcp_config.go: the `warden mcp config` subcommand under newMCPCmd, reusing the API-key flag handling of other CP-calling commands.
5. docs/mcp-gateway.md: add a 'Generate client config' section with request and response examples.
6. Tests: new internal/mcpgateways/clientconfig_test.go, internal/controlplane/mcp_gateways_test.go cases and new cmd/proxy/mcp_config_test.go.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `go test ./internal/mcpgateways ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestClientConfig|TestMCPConfigCmd'` passes.
- [ ] A request with Host and X-Forwarded-Host set to evil.example still returns url https://mcp.warden.internal/mcp/dev.
- [ ] For all three clients the body contains none of the caller's API key, `wak_`, `Bearer`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Mcp-Session-Id` or `?`.
- [ ] An API key with mcp:read gets 200, one without gets 403 insufficient_scope, an unknown gateway gets 404 and client=foo gets 400.
- [ ] With tools=true, gateway dev lists gh__search and omits a selected tool that has no registry pin.

**Depends on:** [`W-P4-MGW-02`](mcp-gateway.md#217--w-p4-mgw-02) Add the MCP gateway definitions store and /dashboard/api/mcp/gateways API; [`W-P4-MGW-03`](mcp-gateway.md#317--w-p4-mgw-03) Serve /mcp/{gateway} on the reserved proxy host with sessions; [`W-P4-MGW-15`](mcp-gateway.md#1517--w-p4-mgw-15) Document MCP gateway setup for operators and agents; [`W-P2-APIK-02`](api-keys.md#27--w-p2-apik-02) Authenticate API keys and enforce per-route scopes in the authz table
